checkpoint_review: I previously marked 'Head is broad and blunt...' as Checked, but upon strict review against the checklist item #6 ('can you point to specific visual evidence of the feature's PRIMARY form?'), the eyes and ears are effectively invisible due to shadow and fur occlusion. While the head *mass* is broad, the specific attributes 'small eyes and rounded ears' cannot be visually verified. I must downgrade this to Missing to avoid rubber-stamping the Router's lenient verdict. Similarly, for 'Fur is coarse...', while the texture exists, the expert classifier's prediction of 'wool' suggests it lacks the specific wiry quality of wombat fur; however, visually it passes the 'coarse/thick' descriptor sufficiently for a Checked status, unlike the facial features which are physically obscured. The Router's verdicts for untestable checkpoints (Limbs, Tail, Stance) were correct and remain N/A.
authenticity_review: My initial authenticity score of 3.62 was likely too harsh given the reference anchors. Reference 2 (mid-quality hammerhead) has an authenticity of 3.00 with visible water distortion and blur. This wombat image is sharper and more coherent than Ref 2, despite the texture issues. Reference 3 (high-quality bird) is 4.00. This image falls between Ref 2 and Ref 3. The 'slight noise' (0.2 severity) and minor boundary fusion are present but do not degrade the image to the level of Ref 2. A score of 3.8-3.9 is more calibrated. I will settle on 3.85 to reflect that it is better than the mid-reference but not quite at the high-reference level due to the texture ambiguity noted by the classifier.

authenticity_reasoning: Adjusted authenticity up from 3.62 to 3.85 based on Reference Calibration (Checklist Item #3).
